page: Microsoft Azure D32as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the Dav6 family, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration provides 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512 (f, vnni, bf16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. It includes 128.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance does not include discrete GPUs and possesses no local storage, requiring network-attached remote storage solutions.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-core and vectorized compute capacity. The server recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 2008.0 and a multi-core score of 16501.0, both placing in the top 25%. In stress-ng, single-core CPU throughput reached 3081.07 (top 25%), while multi-core throughput registered 49300.64 in the middle 50%. PassMark tests reflect similar trends, producing a strong encryption score of 38601.6 and a memory score of 2795.42, against a mid-tier overall CPU score of 46735.41. In vectorized image and text processing tests, the instance performed in the top 25%, while ray tracing and software compilation tasks fell within median boundaries.

Data handling and memory throughput follow an expected enterprise profile. Uncached large-block (256 MB) memory bandwidth measured 79.93 GB/sec for reads and 59.23 GB/sec for writes, both falling within the middle 50% category, while cached small-block reads peaked at 2432.65 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 44.56 million Redis SET operations per second and 28.14 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. On CPU-driven machine learning inference, the instance demonstrated strong performance on lightweight 135M parameter models (2668.32 prompt tokens/sec and 329.08 generation tokens/sec), moderating to 90.47 prompt tokens/sec on 7B models.

From an architectural standpoint, the D32as_v6 provides reliable multi-threaded compute efficiency balanced with high memory density. Because local storage is absent, disk I/O depends entirely on external storage network throughput. This configuration suits medium-to-large relational databases, distributed caching layers, application backends, container orchestration nodes, and continuous integration pipelines that benefit from balanced resources without needing local scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure D32as_v6 is a general-purpose instance featuring 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor at 3.7 GHz. Equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, it adheres to a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The architecture incorporates advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 extensions and VAES, but contains no local storage or GPUs. Performance testing demonstrates strong single-core compute and encryption capabilities, complemented by solid Geekbench multi-core and memory sub-scores. In memory and web-serving benchmarks, the machine consistently operates in the middle tier, delivering 44.56 million Redis operations per second and 28.14 GB/sec web throughput. CPU inference is efficient for small language models but tapers off as model size increases. The D32as_v6 is suitable for enterprise application tiers, web serving clusters, database workloads, and CI/CD pipelines relying on remote persistent storage.
